# PART I: Foundations of LBBNN & Input-Skip Architecture (ISLaB)

## Motivation — Why Sparse & Explainable BNNs in Official Statistics?

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Black-Box \& Over-Parameterization Dilemma:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Modern deep neural networks capture complex multi-way interactions, but lack calibrated uncertainty quantification and interpretable feature attributions.
  \item Standard dense BNNs quantify parameter uncertainty, but retain all noise covariates, inflating variance in downstream survey estimators.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.5em}
\textbf{What Official Statistics Requires:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Structural Sparsity}: Combine model selection (spike-and-slab edge pruning) and parameter uncertainty in a single variational framework.
  \item \textbf{Explainable Depth}: Automatically adapt between simple linear GLMs ($\text{Depth} = 1$) and deep non-linear interaction surfaces ($\text{Depth} > 1$).
  \item \textbf{Survey \& Privacy Rigor}: Rigorous integration with informative sampling weights, differential privacy ($\epsilon, \delta$), and non-probability samples.
\end{itemize}

## From Dense BNNs to Latent Binary BNNs (Hubin & Storvik, 2024)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Spike-and-Slab Edge Selection:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Latent binary inclusion indicator $\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} \in \{0, 1\}$:
  \small
  $$p\big(w_{k,p}^{(j)} \mid \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\mathcal{N}\big(0, (\tau_{k,p}^{(j)})^2\big) + \big(1-\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)\delta_0$$
  $$p\big(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \text{Bernoulli}\big(\psi_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA)}: Ensembles across posterior draws $\Gamma \sim q(\Gamma)$ and $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma)$ for optimal uncertainty quantification.
  \item \textbf{Median Probability Model (MPM)}: Hard-prunes edges with posterior inclusion probability $a_{k,p}^{(j)} \le 0.5$ (Barbieri \& Berger, 2004 optimal predictive submodel).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Input-Skip LBBNNs (ISLaB) & Structural Depth Metrics (Høyheim et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{The ISLaB Architecture (\textit{JAIR}, 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Direct skips route inputs $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ to every hidden layer: $\mathbf{a}^{(j-1)} = [a_1^{(j-1)}, \dots, a_K^{(j-1)}, \mathbf{x}^\top]^\top$.
  \item \textbf{Active Path ($\text{AP}$)}: Connects input $x_k$ to output $\zeta$ via edges with $a_{k,p}^{(j)} > 0.5$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Contribution Depth Classification:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Depth = 1}: Direct skip $\implies$ linear GLM effect.
  \item \textbf{Depth $\ge$ 2}: Hidden layers $\implies$ non-linear interaction.
  \item \textbf{Paths = 0}: Noise covariate pruned from graph.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}

## Local Explainability via Polyhedral ReLU Activation Regions

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Local GLM Theorem (JSM 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Piecewise-linear activations partition $\mathbb{R}^p$ into polyhedral activation regions $\mathcal{P}_1, \dots, \mathcal{P}_M$.
  \item Within each local region $\mathcal{P}_m$, the active network reduces to an exact \textbf{local GLM}:
  \small
  $$\zeta(\mathbf{x}) = \beta_0(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{j=1}^p \beta_j(\mathbf{x}_i) x_j$$
  $$\boldsymbol{\beta}(\mathbf{x}_i) = \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \zeta(\mathbf{x})\big|_{\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}_i}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Gradients}: Evaluated via analytical backpropagation (zero perturbation error).
  \item \textbf{Credible Intervals}: Draws $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma^*)$ yield exact posterior intervals for respondent sensitivities.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_polyhedral_regions.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Variational Inference & Protection Against Cold Posteriors

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Variational ELBO at True $T = 1.0$:}
\small
$$\text{ELBO}(q) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}_{q}[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)] - \text{KL}(q \parallel p)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Why Explicit Error Scale $\sigma^2$ Matters (Wenzel et al., 2020):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Omitting residual noise scale $\sigma^2$ artificially rescales likelihood ($T = \sigma^2 \neq 1$), mis-calibrating spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item In \texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma = ...)}, calibrated $\sigma^2$ grounds log-likelihood sensitivities on the true Bayesian scale.
  \item Calibrates both feature inclusion probabilities $a_k$ and DP sensitivities $f_i$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_variational_elbo.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART II: Track 1 — Unit-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors & Formal Differential Privacy

## Unit-Weighted Variational Pseudo-Posteriors (Savitsky & Toth, 2016)

\vspace{0.2em}
Equipping each unit $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ with a non-negative weight $u_i \ge 0$ defines the pseudo-posterior:
\small
$$p_{\mathbf{u}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}) \propto p(\theta) \prod_{i=1}^n f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)^{u_i}$$
$$\text{ELBO}(q; \mathbf{u}) = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \, \mathbb{E}_{q(\theta)}\!\left[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)\right] - \text{KL}\big(q(\theta) \parallel p(\theta)\big)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{1. Survey Sampling Weights ($u_i = \tilde{w}_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Normalized to sample size $n$: $\tilde{w}_i = w_i \frac{n}{\sum w_j}$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = TRUE} ensures $\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$ does not overpower spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item Corrects informative sampling selection bias.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{2. Differential Privacy Weights ($u_i = \alpha_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Unnormalized weights: $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = FALSE} ensures $\sum \alpha_i \le n$.
  \item Downweights high-sensitivity tail outliers and contracts the pseudo-posterior toward the prior.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1A — Informative Survey Sampling Setup & Automated Noise Pruning

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 2,000, p = 4$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{True Non-Linear DGP}:
  \small
  $$Y_i = 2 X_{1i} + 1.5 \sin(\pi X_{2i}) + 0.8 X_{1i} X_{2i} + \varepsilon_i$$
  \normalsize
  where $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.4^2)$, and $X_3, X_4 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ are pure noise.
  \item \textbf{Informative Selection Mechanism}:
  \small
  $$\pi_i = \text{logit}^{-1}(-1.0 + 1.2 Y_i)$$
  \normalsize
  Draws $n = 737$ units favoring high $Y_i$.
  \item Unweighted sample mean is \textbf{+2.009} (True population mean: \textbf{0.000}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Track 1A — Domain Estimation, Imputation & Dirichlet Bootstrap UQ

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Domain Totals \& De-Noising:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Domain Membership Matrix} $\mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times D_{\text{dom}}}$ defines sub-populations (industries, regions):
  \small
  $$\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{BNN}(s)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i G_{i,d} \, \hat{\mu}_i^{(s)}}{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i G_{i,d}}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Removing Observation Noise}: Using latent conditional mean $\hat{\mu}_i^{(s)} = \mu_{\theta^{(s)}}(\mathbf{x}_i)$ explicitly strips additive measurement error $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$, recovering pure regression surfaces.
  \item \textbf{Item Non-Response Imputation}: Missing outcomes ($y_i = \text{NA}$) are filled via posterior predictive draws $\tilde{y}_i^{(s)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{\theta^{(s)}}(\mathbf{x}_i), \sigma^2)$ (\texttt{impute\_response\_lbbnn}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Dirichlet Bayesian Bootstrap UQ:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{The Pseudo-Posterior Variance Deficit}: Pseudo-posteriors condition on fixed sample $S$, underestimating design-based sampling variance.
  \item \textbf{Dirichlet Perturbations} (Savitsky \& Toth, 2016): For each draw $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$, sample flat Dirichlet perturbations:
  \small
  $$\boldsymbol{\xi}^{(s)} = (\xi_1^{(s)}, \dots, \xi_n^{(s)}) \sim \text{Dirichlet}(1, \dots, 1)$$
  $$\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{(s)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^{(s)} w_i G_{i,d} \, y_i^{(s)}}{\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^{(s)} w_i G_{i,d}}$$
  \normalsize
  \item Restores exact finite-population frequentist coverage in credible intervals (\texttt{dirichlet\_uq = TRUE}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Pipeline & Return Structures: Survey-Weighted LBBNN (Track 1A)

\vspace{-0.3em}
\scriptsize
```r
# 1. Package design weights & allow missing response values (y_i = NA)
dl_train <- get_dataloaders(df_survey, weights = w_design, normalize_weights = TRUE,
                            allow_missing = TRUE, train_batch_size = 64, test_batch_size = 32)
# 2. Build LBBNN with calibrated residual noise scale sigma (protects T=1)
net <- lbbnn_net(problem_type = "regression", sizes = c(p, 16, 1), sigma = 0.4, input_skip = TRUE)
fit <- train_lbbnn(LBBNN = net, train_dl = dl_train$train_loader, epochs = 100, lr = 0.01)
# 3. Domain predictions & Bayesian imputation with Dirichlet uncertainty draws
dom_est <- predict_domains_lbbnn(net, X, domain_matrix = G, weights = w_design,
                                 type = "latent_mean", dirichlet_uq = TRUE, draws = 50)
imp_res <- impute_response_lbbnn(net, newdata = df_survey, target_col = "y", draws = 50)
```
\normalsize

## Track 1B — Why Unweighted Neural Networks Fail Differential Privacy

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Probabilistic Differential Privacy (Savitsky, Williams \& Hu, 2022):}
\small
$$\sup_{\theta \in \Theta_\delta} \left|\log \frac{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y})}{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}')}\right| \le \epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2 \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}, \qquad \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s, i} |\alpha_i \log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta^{(s)})|$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{The Quadratic Exposure Dilemma in Gaussian Regression:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pointwise Gaussian log-likelihood grows quadratically with the residual:
  $$|\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)| \propto \frac{(y_i - \mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))^2}{2\sigma^2}$$
  \item In skewed survey microdata (wages, financial expenditures), extreme outliers drive unweighted sensitivity $\Delta \to \infty$ and privacy budget $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} \to \infty$.
  \item Naive gradient clipping distorts the mean and destroys the variance structure of official statistics.
\end{itemize}

## Track 1B — The Two-Pass Surgical Downweighting Pipeline (`fit_dp_lbbnn`)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.72, every node/.style={scale=0.72, font=\sffamily}]
  \node[rectangle, draw=blue!80, fill=blue!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.4cm, align=center] (p1) at (0, 0) {\textbf{Pass 1}\\[2pt]Unweighted Fit\\[2pt]($u_i = 1$)};
  \node[rectangle, draw=orange!80, fill=orange!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.5cm, align=center] (risk) at (3.4, 0) {\textbf{Extract Risk}\\[2pt]$S \times n$ Matrix $L_{s,i}$\\[2pt]$f_i = \max_s |L_{s,i}|$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=purple!80, fill=purple!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.6cm, align=center] (weight) at (7.0, 0) {\textbf{Surgical Weights}\\[2pt]Smooth $\alpha_i^{\text{raw}}$\\[2pt]Zero Tail Outliers};
  \node[rectangle, draw=green!70!black, fill=green!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.4cm, align=center] (p2) at (10.6, 0) {\textbf{Pass 2}\\[2pt]$\alpha$-Weighted Fit\\[2pt]$\Delta_{\alpha} \le M_{\text{thresh}}$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=red!80, fill=red!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.2cm, align=center] (synth) at (14.0, 0) {\textbf{Synthesis}\\[2pt]$(\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}}, \delta)$-PDP Microdata};
  
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p1) -- (risk);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (risk) -- (weight);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (weight) -- (p2);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p2) -- (synth);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Monotone Surgical Truncation Formula:}
$$\alpha_i = \min\!\left(\alpha_i^{\text{raw}}, \, \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{f_i}\right), \qquad \alpha_i = 0 \quad \text{if } f_i > 3 M_{\text{thresh}}$$
Guarantees local Lipschitz bound $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s,i} |\alpha_i L_{s,i}^{(2)}| \le M_{\text{thresh}}$ and bounded privacy $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}$.

## Track 1B — Monotone Surgical Downweighting Diagnostic

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.60\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/track1_dp_weights.pdf}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.40\textwidth}
\textbf{Empirical DP Metrics:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Sample}: $n = 300$, median $\$4.16$, 3 extreme outliers ($\$400\text{--}\$530$).
  \item \textbf{Standard Records}: Retain high weights $\alpha_i \in [0.34, 0.85]$ (median $0.81$).
  \item \textbf{Tail Outliers}: All 3 outliers ($f_i > 26 > 3M$) surgically zeroed ($\alpha_i = 0.0$).
  \item \textbf{Privacy Guarantee}:\\
  $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = 4.32 \le 5.50 \implies \boldsymbol{\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 8.63}$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1B — Two-Stage Privacy Weight Normalization (Savitsky, 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Record Sensitivity Proxy:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Extract worst-case empirical log-likelihood sensitivity from unweighted Pass 1:
  \small
  $$f_i = \max_{s \in \{1, \dots, S\}} |\ell_i(\theta^{(s)})|, \quad \tilde{\alpha}_i = \frac{1}{f_i}$$
  \normalsize
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Stage 1: Initial Normalization Options:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Global Linear Min-Max} (\texttt{"linear"}):
  \small
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{lin}} = \text{clip}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(c \cdot \frac{\tilde{\alpha}_i - \tilde{\alpha}_{\min}}{\tilde{\alpha}_{\max} - \tilde{\alpha}_{\min}} + g\right)$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Percentile Deficit Truncation} (\texttt{"percentile"}):
  \small
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{pct}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \max\!\left(0, \, \frac{\tilde{\alpha}_i - q_{p_L}(\tilde{\alpha})}{q_{p_R}(\tilde{\alpha}) - q_{p_L}(\tilde{\alpha})}\right)\right)$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Target Ratio Clipping} (\texttt{"target\_clip"}):
  \small
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{clip}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \frac{\Delta_{i, \text{goal}}}{f_i}\right)$$
  \normalsize
\end{enumerate}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Theoretical Properties (Proposition 1):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Min-Max Vulnerability}: Inliers ($f_{j^*} \to 0 \implies \tilde{\alpha}_{\max} \to \infty$) uniformly deflate intermediate sample weights.
  \item \textbf{Percentile Deficit}: Truncates bottom $p_L$ tail risk and boosts intermediate sample size ($\sum \alpha_i$), but requires Stage 2 to bound $\alpha_i f_i$.
  \item \textbf{Exact Sensitivity Control}: Target clipping guarantees $\alpha_i^{\text{clip}} f_i = \min(f_i, \Delta_{\text{goal}}) \le \Delta_{\text{goal}}$ by construction, leaving all low-sensitivity records untouched at $\alpha_i = 1$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1B — Stage 2: Hard Truncation vs. Vector-Weighted Upward Rescaling

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Scheme 1: Hard Truncation (\texttt{"hard\_trunc"}):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Post-hoc zeroing of records exceeding threshold:
  \small
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{trunc}} = \alpha_i \, \mathbb{I}(\alpha_i f_i \le M_{\text{thresh}})$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Limitation}: Single-pass truncation completely discards tail observations and leaves unspent privacy slack $M_{\text{thresh}} - \alpha_i f_i > 0$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Scheme 2: Vector Rescaling (\texttt{"vector\_upscale"}):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Upward rescaling to full threshold capacity:
  \small
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \alpha_i \cdot \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{\alpha_i f_i}\right) = \min\!\left(1, \, \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{f_i}\right)$$
  \normalsize
  \item Pointwise dominates hard truncation: $\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} \ge \alpha_i^{\text{trunc}}$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Information Dominance (Proposition 2):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Because $\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} \ge \alpha_i^{\text{trunc}}$ everywhere, vector upward rescaling strictly maximizes Fisher information:
  \small
  $$\mathcal{I}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\text{vec}}}(\theta) \succeq \mathcal{I}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\text{trunc}}}(\theta)$$
  \normalsize
  in the Loewner partial order.
  \item \textbf{Pass 3 Execution}: Upward rescaling shifts pseudo-posterior geometry $\xi_{\alpha^{\text{vec}}}(\theta \mid D)$; \texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn} executes an additional variational pass targeting $\xi_{\alpha^{\text{vec}}}$ to ensure calibration and bound verification.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART III: Track 2 — Combining Probability & Non-Probability Samples

## The Big Data Paradox in Convenience Samples (Meng, 2018)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Non-Probability Selection Dilemma:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Let $U = \{1, \dots, N\}$ denote the finite target population of size $N$.
  \item In convenience/opt-in samples $S_c \subset U$, sample inclusion $I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$ is non-random and driven by unobserved self-selection mechanisms.
  \item \textbf{Meng's Law of Large Populations (2018)}:
  \small
  $$\text{Bias}(\bar{y}_c) = \frac{\text{Cov}_U(I_c, Y)}{\bar{\pi}_c} = \rho_{I_c, Y} \cdot \sigma_Y \cdot \sqrt{\frac{N - n_c}{n_c}}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Definitions}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\pi_{ci} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ci} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)$: Unknown propensity that unit $i$ with covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ self-selects into $S_c$.
    \item $\bar{\pi}_c = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i \in U} \pi_{ci}$: Average participation propensity across the entire target population $U$.
  \end{itemize}
  \item A tiny correlation $\rho_{I_c, Y} \neq 0$ creates selection bias scaling with $\sqrt{N}$; increasing sample size $n_c$ merely concentrates error around a severely biased estimate.
\end{itemize}

## The Identification Barrier & The Conditioning Trick (Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\textbf{The Identification Barrier:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ are observed only on convenience sample $S_c$ (unknown $\pi_{ci}$) and reference survey $S_r$ (known design probability $\pi_{ri}$). Non-sampled units $U \setminus (S_c \cup S_r)$ are never observed.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Conditioning Trick \& Structural Offset Derivation:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pool $S_c$ and $S_r$ into a combined sample $S$, and model membership indicator $D_i = \mathbb{I}(i \in S_c)$:
  \small
  $$\pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}} = \mathbb{P}(D_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i, i \in S) = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Step-by-Step Log-Odds (Logit) Expansion}:
  \small
  $$\log\left(\frac{\pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}}}{1 - \pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}}}\right) = \log\left(\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ri}}\right) = \log \pi_{ci} - \log \pi_{ri} = \eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) - \log \pi_{ri}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Structural Offset}: Because $\pi_{ri}$ is known by survey design, $-\log \pi_{ri}$ enters as an \textbf{exact, fixed offset} in the binary cross-entropy loss, anchoring unconstrained neural network logits $\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)$ to the true population scale.
\end{itemize}

## Intuition & Torch Training Link for All Five Estimators

\vspace{0.1em}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.20}
\scriptsize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{0.13\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}p{0.36\textwidth}}
\toprule
\textbf{Estimator} & \textbf{Sample Overlap} & \textbf{Composite Prob $\pi_{zi}$} & \textbf{Torch Backprop \& Loss Link} \\
\midrule
\texttt{STACK} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Unlinked) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ & Offset $\text{logit}(\pi_{zi}) = \eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) - \log \pi_{ri}$ in Bernoulli NLL. \\
\texttt{LINK1} & $S_c \cup (S_r \setminus S_c)$ & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}}$ & Deduplicated union; backprops through $-\pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}$ overlap adjustment. \\
\texttt{LINK2} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Linked Stack) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}(1 + \pi_{ri})}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ & Exact indicator $I_{zi} = D_i + (1-D_i)I_{ci}$; maximizes Fisher info. \\
\texttt{MIP} & Missing Information & Bridges \texttt{STACK} \& \texttt{LINK2} & Evaluates expectation $\tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1-D_i)\tilde{p}_i$ with $\tilde{p}_i \in [0, 1]$. \\
\texttt{PSEUDO} & Survey-Weighted & Design pseudo-likelihood & Score: $\sum_{S_r} \pi_{ri}^{-1}\text{softplus}(\eta_i) + \sum_{S_c} \log(1 + e^{-\eta_i}) = 0$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

\vspace{-0.3em}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Composite vs. Pseudo}: Composite likelihoods (\texttt{STACK}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{MIP}) form relative odds fractions that naturally bound loss gradients, whereas \texttt{PSEUDO} multiplies unconstrained logits by $\pi_{ri}^{-1}$.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## Where Marginal Linkage Weights $\tilde{p}_i$ Come From in MIP

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Probabilistic Record Linkage Origin:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item In agency applications, deterministic matching is often precluded by privacy regulations or noisy identifiers (names, addresses).
  \item An auxiliary probabilistic record linkage model (e.g., Fellegi-Sunter) estimates pairwise match probabilities:
  \small
  $$m_{ij} = \mathbb{P}(i \sim j \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j) \in [0, 1]$$
  \normalsize
  \item Marginalizing across reference candidates yields each unit's linkage probability:
  \small
  $$\tilde{p}_i = \sum_{j \in S_r} m_{ij} \in [0, 1]$$
  \normalsize
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Vectorized Unit Linkage in `LBBNN`:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Analysts supply the unit-level linkage vector:
  \small
  $$\tilde{\mathbf{p}} = (\tilde{p}_1, \dots, \tilde{p}_n)^\top$$
  \normalsize
  directly into \texttt{make\_nll\_mip(p\_link = p\_vec)}.
  \item \textbf{Adaptive Gradient Pull}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item High-certainty matches ($\tilde{p}_i \approx 1$) pull gradient updates toward the low-variance \texttt{LINK2} surface.
    \item Ambiguous/unmatched units ($\tilde{p}_i \approx 0$) safely revert to the robust \texttt{STACK} formulation.
  \end{itemize}
  \item Smoothly bridges deterministic linkage and unlinked stacking record-by-record.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Study 0 — Exact Linear Baseline Monte Carlo ($R = 20$, Visual Benchmark)

\includegraphics[width=0.91\textwidth]{figures/track2_study0_rmse_bars.pdf}

\vspace{-0.1em}
\textbf{Empirical Findings, The Oracle Benchmark, \& Stein's Phenomenon}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{The Oracle Benchmark}: Theoretical bound plugging true data-generating propensities $\pi_{ci}$ directly into H\'{a}jek weighting (bypassing propensity estimation).
  \item \textbf{Why LBBNN Beats the Oracle in Panel B (Low Support)}: Under low common support, true propensities near 0 create extreme $1/\pi_{ci}$ weights and high sampling variance. \texttt{LBBNN} regularization smooths tail weights, trading tiny bias for a large variance reduction (Stein's phenomenon).
  \item \textbf{Pseudo-Likelihood Breakdown}: Under low support, \texttt{GLM-PSEUDO} explodes to $\text{RMSE} = 1.015$ (weight variance and gradient explosion), while composite formulations remain bounded ($\text{RMSE} \approx 0.16\text{--}0.33$).
\end{itemize}

## Study 1 — Automated Confounder Selection & Noise Pruning ($p = 6$)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.42\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 5,000, p = 6$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Confounders}: $X_1, X_2$ drive both propensity $\pi_{ci}$ and outcome $Y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Outcome-Only}: $X_3$ drives $Y_i$ but uncorrelated with selection $I_c$.
  \item \textbf{Pure Noise}: $X_4, X_5, X_6 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Why Variable Selection Matters}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item In propensity modeling, forcing outcome-only $X_3$ does \textbf{not} reduce selection bias, but \textbf{inflates H\'{a}jek weight variance}.
  \item \texttt{LBBNN} automatically prunes $X_3$ ($\alpha_3 = 0.028 \ll 0.50$) along with pure noise $X_4\text{--}X_6$, isolating true selection confounders ($X_1, X_2$).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Pipeline & Return Structures: Composite Propensity (Track 2)

\vspace{-0.3em}
\scriptsize
```r
# 1. Format combined sample with vectorized linkage probabilities p_vec
prep    <- build_propensity_dataset(pop, method = "MIP", covar_cols = paste0("X", 1:p), p_link = p_vec_r)
dl_prop <- get_dataloaders(prep$data, target_cols = prep$target_cols, train_batch_size = 64, test_batch_size = 32)
# 2. Fit LBBNN with composite Bernoulli loss anchored by pi_ri offset
net_prop <- lbbnn_net(problem_type = "custom", sizes = c(p, 8, 1), raw_output = TRUE, nll = make_nll_mip())
train_lbbnn(LBBNN = net_prop, train_dl = dl_prop$train_loader, epochs = 150, lr = 0.02)
# 3. Predict convenience propensities pi_c_hat & compute debiased Hajek mean
logits_c    <- predict(net_prop, newdata = prep$data[prep$Sc_indices, 1:p], mpm = TRUE)
pi_c_hat    <- as.numeric(torch::torch_sigmoid(torch::torch_tensor(logits_c)))
y_bar_hajek <- hajek_estimate(y = pop$y[pop$I.c == 1], pi_hat = pi_c_hat, dirichlet_uq = TRUE)
```

## Discussion — Bridging Track 2 Propensity Weights with Track 1 Regression

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Two-Stage Quasi-Randomization (Track 2):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Stage 1}: \texttt{LBBNN} propensity model estimates $\hat{\pi}_{ci} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ci} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)$.
  \item \textbf{Stage 2}: Apply outcome-agnostic H\'{a}jek weights:
  \small
  $$\hat{w}_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1}, \qquad \hat{\bar{Y}}_{\text{Hajek}} = \frac{\sum_{i \in S_c} \hat{w}_i y_i}{\sum_{i \in S_c} \hat{w}_i}$$
  \normalsize
  to any survey response variable $y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Outcome-Only Sparsity}: Pruning $X_3$ (which predicts $Y$ but not $I_c$) prevents weight variance inflation.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Doubly Robust Pseudo-Posterior Imputation:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Bridging Track 2 $\to$ Track 1}: Normalize inverse propensity weights to sample size:
  \small
  $$\tilde{w}_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1} \frac{n_c}{\sum_{j \in S_c} \hat{\pi}_{cj}^{-1}}$$
  \normalsize
  and feed $u_i = \tilde{w}_i$ directly into a \textbf{Track 1 LBBNN regression model} for $y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Double Robustness}: Consistent if \emph{either} propensity model \emph{or} outcome regression is correctly specified.
  \item Outcome model retains $X_3$ via spike-and-slab, recovering optimal predictive accuracy!
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

  \item \textbf{Survey-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors (Track 1A)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Normalizing survey weights to sample size ($\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$) + calibrated observation noise $\sigma^2$ prevents likelihood mis-scaling ($T \neq 1$) and protects spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
      \item \texttt{LBBNN} achieves 5x lower population RMSE than classical H\'{a}jek weighting under informative sampling while pruning irrelevant covariates.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Two-Pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PDP Microdata Synthesis (Track 1B)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Monotone surgical downweighting and vector upward rescaling (\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn}) eliminate disclosure risk from extreme tail outliers ($\alpha_i = 0$) while preserving high utility ($\alpha_i \in [0.34, 0.85]$) on normal records.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Composite Non-Probability Sample Integration (Track 2)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Conditioning on pooled sample inclusion $S_c \cup S_r$ allows known design probabilities $\pi_{ri}$ to anchor neural network logits to the true population scale.
      \item Composite Bernoulli likelihoods (\texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{MIP}, \texttt{STACK}) bound loss gradients and prevent the catastrophic effective sample size collapse (\texttt{Kish ESS} $< 7$) of pseudo-likelihood under low common support.
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
